text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall: sustained increase in 5xx errors for inference-api in us-west-2c (usw2c). Threshold breached: 10m error rate 12% (baseline 0.4%). Pager: https://pd.example/incident/INC-3219

alice: ack, I'm on it. seeing a big spike of 502/504 from the ELB logs. can't reach a subset of targets. starting root check.

jamal: looking at target group -> targets flapping Unhealthy -> Healthy several times. ELB logs show TCP_CONN_RESET and backend connection timeout.

alice: also seeing EBS I/O errors in instance syslogs: "ext4: nfs_read: I/O error" (paste below)
```
Mar 26 02:22:10 i-0abc123 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme1n1, sector 123456
Mar 26 02:22:12 i-0abc123 kernel: Buffer I/O error on dev nvme1n1, logical block 15432
```

sre-oncall: moving to #incidents-bridge. initial hypothesis: regional EBS / host-level disk issues causing target health failures => ELB resets => Route53 weight fluctuations. We should mitigate by shifting traffic out of usw2c and using fallback nodes in usw2a/usw2b.

natalie: prepared a Route53 change: reduce weight for inference-usw2c to 0, distribute to usw2a/usw2b 50/50. ready to apply if SRE gives :thumbsup:. Change script: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://shift-weight.json`

jamal: confirmed EBS latency on multiple instances in usw2c: DescribeVolumes shows avg read latency 180-250ms. Some volumes report "io.optimized" flag toggled in cloudtrail around event time.

alice: applying Route53 weight shift now to stop customer-facing errors. executing change.

incident-bot: Route53 change initiated (change id CID-5467). TTLs respected: 60s.

support-eng: creating customer-facing banner now. TAG: partial degraded performance for inference in us-west-2c; affects 8-15% of requests with 502/504. Ticket: TW-7893.

aws-bot: Opened AWS Support case 9876543210 for EBS degradation in us-west-2c, attaching instance IDs and kernel logs. ETA initial response 12 minutes.

alice: Route53 weights propagated, traffic away from usw2c dropping. immediate error rate falling from 12% -> 3% in the next 90s. good.

jamal: continuing host remediation: mark problem instances OUT of target group, terminate/replace if EBS remains degraded. Starting automated terminate for instances failing >3 health checks in 5m.

natalie: spun up additional capacity in usw2a/usw2b and pre-warmed model caches; readiness checks passing.

sre-oncall: note -- we bumped ELB healthy threshold to 10s > 2 checks to reduce noisy flaps temporarily (will revert later). Documenting change: ELB health check interval 10s, healthy threshold 2 -> 20s window.

ops-lead: handoff note: night oncall (Ops) will pick this up at 03:00 UTC. ensure AWS case id and change id included in handoff.

alice: AWS responded: "We've identified elevated EBS backend latency in us-west-2c impacting a subset of customers. We're performing remediation on platform side." AWS suggests detaching/reattaching volumes may help but will coordinate if they perform host-level repairs.

support-eng: posted customer update (internal copy): "We detected increased errors for a subset of requests routed to us-west-2c starting ~02:20 UTC. We've moved traffic to other AZs and spun up fallback capacity; customers may see increased latency briefly. We're monitoring and will update when AWS finishes remediation."

jamal: remediation actions performed: 6 instances in target group terminated and replaced; 4 volumes detached and reattached; healthchecks stable. ELB 5xx rate now under 1% global.

sre-oncall: Summary for incident notes (to be used in postmortem): cause: regional EBS performance degradation in us-west-2c causing target health failures and ELB connection resets. impact: partial — ~8-15% of requests observed 5xx for ~40 minutes. mitigation: Route53 weight shift off usw2c, scale-up in other AZs, terminate/replace noisy hosts, AWS engaged for remediation. customer comms: banner + support tickets created.

ops-lead: assigning owners for postmortem items: 1) infra -> evaluate autoscaling & target replacement timing (jamal) 2) platform -> add improved early detection for EBS latency (alice) 3) support -> update customer templates for regional degradation (support-eng).

sre-oncall: handing off to night oncall (ops) at 03:00 UTC. all runbooks and AWS case links in PagerDuty incident. If error rate creeps >2% please escalate back to SRE.

alice: final note before handoff: I saved all ELB target logs and instance kernel logs to s3://redwood-incidents/1768129999/ and attached to PD incident.

incident-bot: Incident incident:INC-3219 transitioned to status: mitigated by sre-oncall.

support-eng: closing customer banner to "monitoring". will reopen if regression.

ops-lead: thanks team. we'll draft postmortem with timeline and RCA.

sre-oncall: thanks all, handing off. :white_check_mark:
